headline: Approved minor plan modification for SK Autobody at 348 Howe St and granted Special Permit for 298 Merrimack St redevelopment
summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a minor plan modification to a previously approved Special Permit for SK Autobody LLC at 348 Howe St. The Board also granted a Special Permit to Madhuben Patel, Trustee of K&K Realty Trust, to reconstruct a nonconforming structure for retail use at 298 Merrimack St. Minutes from the July 22, 2026 meeting were also accepted.
decisions: Accepted the minutes of the July 22, 2026 meeting.
Approved the minor plan modification to the Special Permit for SK Autobody LLC/M.K. Howe Street Realty Trust at 348 Howe St, by roll call vote 5-0.
Approved the Special Permit application 2026-12 for Madhuben Patel, Trustee of K&K Realty Trust, to reconstruct a pre-existing non-conforming structure at 298 Merrimack St, by roll call vote 5-0.

TRANSCRIPT OF PUBLIC RECORD 
ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS MEETING 
August 26, 2026 
 
This Regular Meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals, was held in The Great Hall, 41 Pleasant Street, Methuen 
MA. The meeting was called to order at: 7:00 PM.   
 
Chairman Matthew D’Agostino asked for a moment of silence in memory for all those who have died for our 
country, and led the pledge of allegiance.  
 
MEMBERS IN ATTENDANCE: 
Mr. Matthew D’Agostino, Chairman 
Mr. Nicholas Boucher, Vice Chairman 
Mr. Jose Frias, Clerk 
Mr. Vincenzo Pesce, Member 
Mr. Mansour Chaya, Alternate Member 
Mr. William Haneffant, Alternate Member 
Mr. Matteo Zingales, Alternate Member 
 
Also, In Attendance: 
Joseph Salamone, Building Commissioner 
Lori Moriarty HHSI Clerk III 
Petitioners and Representatives 
 
MEMBERS ABSENT: 
Mr. Philip Cultrera, Member 
 
ROLL OF APPLICANTS:  
 SK Autobody LLC/M.K. Howe Street Realty Trust- present 
Madhuben Patel, Trustee of K&K Realty Trust- present  
 
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES: 
1. July 22, 2026 
 
Mansour Chaya made a motion to accept the minutes of July 22, 2026.  William Haneffant seconded.  
DISCUSSION: NONE 
VOTE: UNANIMOUS  
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
Request for Determination and Approval of Minor Plan Modification to approved Special Permit: 
2025-08 SK Autobody LLC/M.K. Howe Street Realty Trust 
Special Permit previously approved to extend an existing nonconforming use of 
Autobody/Auto Repair at 348 HOWE ST, METHUEN MA 01844 
 
Attorney Anthony Copani with office location of 265 Broadway in Methuen, came forward representing 
the petitioner.  A Special Permit was approved last July by the Board, to extend a nonconforming use to 
the autobody shop, adding a garage to an existing garage. They are seeking a minor plan revision, to the
Page 2 of 4 
 
plan previously approved.  The proposed revised plan would separate the building by 12 feet and shift 
the new garage 12 feet in another direction. They maintain that the proposed changes are not 
substantive, and that that these substantive factors have already been addressed by the Board with the 
approval of the Special Permit, including traffic, parking, effect on the neighborhood, abutters etc.  
 
Dave Jordan, Engineer and land surveyor with GPI, came forward to review the changes.    The plan, 
seen on the easel which was also provided to the Board, shows that they will be moving the proposed 
garage over 12 feet from the existing garage.  The plan in the approved Special permit, had the proposed 
new garage attached to the existing garage.  After discussions with the building department, and 
discovering that attaching the new building would result in a myriad of other requirements with regards 
to access and the fire department, they came to an agreement on a plan that would be more feasible.   
 
David Jordan handed out to the Board a sketch showing the overlay of the approved plan and the new 
plan.  The image in black is the plan approved by the Board and the image in red shows how the new 
proposed building would shift to the west.  The pavement did not change, only the loss of 1 parking 
space. Nothing else moved.  They believe the new garage plan is a minor change to what was already 
approved.  
 
Chairman Matt D’Agostino opened up the floor for questions from the Board. There were no questions 
at that time.  
 
Attorney Copani came forward again. Chairman D’Agostino asked what the main reason for the change.   
Attorney Copani stated that there are several and the most pressing being the construction cost.  
Requirements with the attached building sets into motion a number of other approvals that would make 
the project financially unfeasible.   
 
The Chairman opened public participation. No one came forward in favor or opposition. 
The Chairman closed public participation.  
 
There were no other questions from Board members. The Chairman called for a roll call vote. 
 
ROLL CALL VOTE:   
 
Matthew D’Agostino: yes 
Nicholas Boucher: yes 
Jose Frias: yes 
Matteo Zingales: yes 
Vincenzo Pesce: yes 
 
Application for Special Permit: 
 
2026-12 Madhuben Patel, Trustee of K&K Realty Trust 
A Special Permit is required from the Zoning Board of Appeals under Section IX-D of the 
City of Methuen Zoning Ordinance to reconstruct a pre-existing non-conforming structure 
located at 298 Merrimack St, Methuen MA . in the “BN” Neighborhood Business 
zone. The proposed structure is approximately 4,200 sq. ft of retail space defined as small 
retail and allowed by right under Section V -D, and will not meet front and rear 
setbacks. The property abuts the "RD" Single -Family Residence zone and the additional 
buffer strip required by Section VI-B.12 will not be met. Parcel ID: 1111-108-354
Page 3 of 4 
 
 
Attorney Mark Johnson of Johnson & Borenstein law offices at 12 Chestnut St in Andover came forward, 
representing the petitioner . Also, in attendance was Frank Patel principal for K&K Realty Trust, the 
project engineer, Mr. Ian Ainslie and Jonathan Stark-Sachs from Johnson & Borenstein.  Attorney Johnson 
went through a  brief Power Point for the Board outlining the proposed project.  The project requires a 
Special permit from the Zoning Board for a redevelopment of the property on 298 Merrimack St.  They 
have already been in front City council for rezoning, as well as the Planning Board who made 
recommendations to City Council.  The rezoning has been approved through City Council, which includes 
2 parcels of land abutting by common ownership. They will be taking part of that residential lot and 
making it commercial, to be included in this projec t.  His client owns both parcels of land, abutting the 
commercial site. Attorney Johnson said that they believe only a Special Permit is needed because it is a 
redevelopment of an existing non- conforming site and they maintain they will not be making the non-
conformities any worse.  
 
Attorney Johnson displayed the existing site as well as a site plan with the rezoned parcel  area. Also 
displayed was a site plan showing how the proposed building would be situated and an architectural picture 
of the new building. Vehicle access to the parking lot will be from both Arcadia and Merrimack Streets.  
They will have specific curb cuts designated for vehicle access, which will improve traffic flow, since 
right now vehicles can access from anywhere.   
 
Attorney Johnson walked through the Special Permit approval criteria with the Board.  Some items he 
mentioned are removal of a dilapidated building, and improved traffic flow and pedestrian safety. They 
maintained that there will be  no impact with regards to wetlands or the natural environment. They also 
maintain that the project is consistent with The City of Methuen’s master plan, and will provide increased 
tax revenue.   
 
The Chairman opened up the floor for questions from the Board. There were no questions at that time.  
 
The Chairman opened public participation. No one came forward in favor or opposition. 
The Chairman closed public participation.  
 
Chairman D’Agostino opened up the floor for additional questions from the Board.  
 
Inquiries from the Board included the rational on why the setback is so close to the property line.  Mr. 
Ainslie pointed out the existing conditions, showing the current encroachment on Arcadia Street.  They 
will be improving that situation, bringing the new building to 7.5 fee from property line. They also wanted 
to keep the building away from their other abutter at 7 Ames Street and have plenty of parking, improving 
the traffic flow situation. The parking lot will abut the 7 Ames Street address.   
William Haneffant asked if there were going to be any doors on Arcadia Street, questioning if  there may 
be potential traffic and safety issues with loading areas on the side street.  The petitioner confirmed there 
will be no doors on Arcadia, and all deliveries will be through the front entrance.  
The petitioner also confirmed that the property that is infringed on is the same owner. Both residential lots 
and the commercial lot are the same owner. The lot line is in the process of being officially removed and 
will be recorded with Community Development and Registry of Deeds.   
Vincenzo Pesce asked if the use is currently a liquor store, and inquired what material the building will be 
made of.  The petitioner stated that the materials are n ot 100% defined at this time. There will be a g lass 
façade, with the same use as a convenience/liquor store. The store owner also owns the liquor store across 
the street. They only sell beer and wine.  
Nick Boucher asked the hours of operation and Mr. Patel confirmed that the hours will not change and are 
7a-10p M-Sat and Sun 8a-9p. Matteo Zingales inquired about the loading and storage of products.  Mr.
Page 4 of 4 
 
Patel confirmed that loading will be through the front  door and they are hoping to have some sort of 
basement storage. William Haneffant asked if the new building will eliminate people watching Keno from 
their vehicles. The owner stated that they may have a couple television displays set up inside the building, 
but that a lot of people like playing from their car, and that probably won’t be eliminated.  
Nick Boucher stated he thought the plan would be a substantial improvement to the property, and he 
wanted to know if they had a trash or snow removal plan as well as lighting plan.  Mr. Patel stated that 
they have a trash removal picked up every week, and already have a dumpster.  They also have someone 
that uses a bobcat and puts the snow in the truck and removes it from the site. The entire property is already 
almost entirely paved right now. They will be creating green space that they can put snow if they need to.  
Chairman Matt D’Agostino stated that lighting and signs would need to come back before the Board if 
they did not follow zoning regulations.  
 
The applicants are asking for reduced buffer zon e with this Special Permit. Nick Boucher expressed his 
concern if the residential property next door was sold, that the buffer zone on this project would be 
minimal. The petitioner stated that any new owner, if the residential property was sold, would be aware 
there is a commercial space next door.  
 
Board Members expressed their beliefs that this would be a significant improvement to the existing 
building on this site.  Chairman Matt D’Agostino commended the applicant for investing in the City with 
a project this size, and he stated that this may reduce traffic on Pleasant Valley Street and Swan/East 
Street, with residents not having to travel to those areas for this type of service.  
 
ROLL CALL VOTE:   
 
Matthew D’Agostino: yes 
Nicholas Boucher: yes 
Jose Frias: Yes 
Mansour Chaya: yes 
Vincenzo Pesce: yes 
 
Nick Boucher and Vincenzo Pesce took a few minutes recognizing the 30 years of dedicated service Matt 
D’Agostino gave to the City of Methuen, as this was his last meeting on the Zoning Board of Appeals.  
Thank you, Matt.  
 
ADJOURNMENT: 
 
There being no further business before the Board, Vincenzo Pesce made a motion to adjourn, and Matteo Zingales 
seconded. 
Discussion: None 
 Vote: Unanimous 
 
Chairman Matthew D’Agostino adjourned the meeting at 7:33 PM. 
 
Respectfully Submitted, 
Lori Moriarty 
City Clerk III HHSI
